translations.literal: The Jing clan—Jing—came from the Gui surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing clan traced its origin to the Gui surname.

sentences.zh: 陳厲公子完適齊，謚曰敬仲，子孫以謚為氏。

translations.literal: Prince Wan, son of Duke Li of Chen, went to Qi; he was given the posthumous title Jing Zhong, and his descendants took the posthumous title as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wan, son of Duke Li of Chen, went to Qi, he received the posthumous name Jing Zhong, and his descendants adopted it as their surname.

sentences.zh: 敬仲之後至秦有敬丕，丕生教，為河東太守，子孫因官家焉。

translations.literal: Among Jing Zhong's descendants in Qin was Jing Pi; Pi fathered Jiao, who served as Administrator of Hedong; the descendants settled there because of his office.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of Jing Zhong in Qin was Jing Pi, whose son Jiao served as Administrator of Hedong; the family established itself there through his post.

sentences.zh: 裔孫韶，漢末為揚州刺史，生昌，封猗氏侯。

translations.literal: A remote descendant Shao, at the end of Han served as Inspector of Yang Province; he fathered Chang, who was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: Their descendant Shao became Inspector of Yang Province in the late Han; his son Chang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yishi.

translations.literal: Chang fathered Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had a son named Gui.

translations.literal: Of the Jing clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Hui.

translations.literal: The Huan clan—Huan—came from the Jiang surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Huan clan traced its origin to the Jiang surname.

translations.literal: Descendants of Duke Huan of Qi took his posthumous title as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: The descendants of Duke Huan of Qi adopted his posthumous title as their surname.

sentences.zh: 又云，出自子姓，宋桓公之後向魋，亦號桓氏。

translations.literal: It is also said they came from the Zi surname: Xiang Kui, descendant of Duke Huan of Song, was also styled the Huan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Another account holds they descended from the Zi line: Xiang Kui, a descendant of Duke Huan of Song, also went by the name Huan.

sentences.zh: 後漢有太子少傅桓榮，世居譙國龍亢。

translations.literal: In Later Han there was Junior Tutor to the Heir Huan Rong, whose family for generations resided at Longkang in Qiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Later Han, Huan Rong served as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; his family had long lived at Longkang in Qiao.

sentences.zh: 榮八世孫彝，晉宣城內史。

translations.literal: Rong's eighth-generation descendant Yi was Interior Secretary of Xuancheng under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations later came Yi, who served Jin as Interior Secretary of Xuancheng.

translations.literal: Five sons: Yun, Wen, Huo, Mi, and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Yun, Wen, Huo, Mi, and Chong.

sentences.zh: 沖，荊州刺史、豐城公，生嗣、謙、修。

translations.literal: Chong, Inspector of Jing Province and Duke of Fengcheng, fathered Si, Qian, and Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, Inspector of Jing Province and Duke of Fengcheng, had sons Si, Qian, and Xiu.

sentences.zh: 修，晉護軍將軍、長社侯，過江居丹楊。

translations.literal: Xiu, Jin General Who Protects the Army and Marquis of Changshe, crossed the Yangtze and settled in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, Jin General Who Protects the Army and Marquis of Changshe, crossed south of the Yangtze and settled in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 生尹，尹生崇之，崇之七世孫法嗣。

translations.literal: He fathered Yin; Yin fathered Chongzhi; Chongzhi's seventh-generation descendant was Fasi.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's line ran through Yin and Chongzhi to Fasi in the seventh generation.

translations.literal: Of the Huan clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Huan clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Yanfan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanfan.

translations.literal: The Zhu clan—Zhu—came from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhu clan traced its origin to the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 周武王克商，封黃帝之後於祝，後為齊所幷，其封域至齊之間祝阿、祝丘是也。

translations.literal: When King Wu of Zhou conquered Shang, he enfeoffed a descendant of the Yellow Emperor at Zhu; later Qi annexed it—the domains between Qi known as Zhu'a and Zhuqiu are this.
translations.idiomatic: After King Wu of Zhou overthrew Shang, he enfeoffed a descendant of the Yellow Emperor at Zhu; Qi later absorbed the state—the region between Qi known as Zhu'a and Zhuqiu marks its old territory.

sentences.zh: 後漢有司徒恬，孫羲生廣，廣為始平太守，子孫留家焉。

translations.literal: In Later Han there was Minister of Works Tian; his grandson Xi fathered Guang, who was Administrator of Shiping; the descendants remained and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: In the Later Han, Tian served as Minister of Works; his grandson Xi's son Guang became Administrator of Shiping, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 生魏太中大夫仍，仍生諶，晉驃騎府司馬。

translations.literal: He fathered Wei Grand Master of Palace Counsel Ren; Ren fathered Chen, Jin Major-in-Chief of the Rapid Cavalry Office.
translations.idiomatic: From Guang came Ren, Grand Master of Palace Counsel under Wei, and Chen, Major-in-Chief of the Rapid Cavalry Office under Jin.

sentences.zh: 諶生偃，散騎常侍，以平關中兵寇，封始平縣伯。

translations.literal: Chen fathered Yan, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; for pacifying banditry in Guanzhong he was enfeoffed as Baron of Shiping county.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's son Yan, a Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, was enfeoffed as Baron of Shiping for quelling unrest in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 生瑜，瑜生熙，熙生寶，三世襲封。

translations.literal: He fathered Yu; Yu fathered Xi; Xi fathered Bao—three generations inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's line continued through Yu and Xi to Bao, with the fief held across three generations.

translations.literal: Two sons: Lao and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had two sons: Lao and Gui.

sentences.zh: 老，後魏輔國將軍、中外都督。

translations.literal: Lao, Northern Wei General Who Assists the State and Director-General of Domestic and Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lao served Northern Wei as General Who Assists the State and Director-General of Domestic and Foreign Affairs.

translations.literal: Two sons: You and Si.
translations.idiomatic: Lao had two sons: You and Si.

translations.literal: Of the Zhu clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhu clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Qinming.
translations.idiomatic: Qinming.

translations.literal: The Ji clan—Ji—came from the Jiang surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji clan traced its origin to the Jiang surname.

sentences.zh: 炎帝之後封於紀，侯爵，為齊所滅，因以國為氏。

translations.literal: A descendant of the Flame Emperor was enfeoffed at Ji as marquis; Qi destroyed the state, and they took the state name as their clan.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of the Flame Emperor was enfeoffed at Ji as a marquis; when Qi destroyed the state, his line took Ji as their surname.

sentences.zh: 隋有司農少卿和整，世居天水上邽，生士騰。

translations.literal: In Sui there was Vice Minister of the Imperial Granary Hezheng, whose family for generations lived at Shanggui in Tianshui; he fathered Shiteng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui, Hezheng served as Vice Minister of the Imperial Granary; his family had long resided at Shanggui in Tianshui, and he had a son Shiteng.

translations.literal: Of the Ji clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Chune.
translations.idiomatic: Chune.

translations.literal: The Zheng clan—Zheng—came from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng clan traced its origin to the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 周厲王少子友封於鄭，是為桓公，其地華州鄭縣是也。

translations.literal: You, younger son of King Li of Zhou, was enfeoffed at Zheng—this was Duke Huan; the territory was Zheng county in Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: You, a younger son of King Li of Zhou, was enfeoffed at Zheng as Duke Huan; his domain lay in Zheng county of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 生武公，與晉文侯夾輔平王，東遷于洛，徙溱、洧之間，謂之新鄭，其地河南新鄭是也。

translations.literal: He fathered Duke Wu, who together with Marquis Wen of Jin jointly assisted King Ping; they moved east to Luo, relocated between the Zhen and Wei rivers—called Xin Zheng—and the territory was Xin Zheng in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duke Wu, together with Marquis Wen of Jin, assisted King Ping in the eastern relocation to Luo; the house moved between the Zhen and Wei rivers to what was called New Zheng—present-day Xin Zheng in Henan.

sentences.zh: 十三世孫幽公為韓所滅，子孫播遷陳、宋之間，以國為氏。

translations.literal: The thirteenth-generation descendant Duke You was destroyed by Han; the descendants scattered between Chen and Song and took the state name as their clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth generation Duke You was extinguished by Han; the clan dispersed through Chen and Song and took Zheng as their surname.

sentences.zh: 幽公生公子魯，魯六世孫榮，號鄭君，生當時，漢大司農，居滎陽開封。

translations.literal: Duke You fathered the lord's son Lu; Lu's sixth-generation descendant Rong, styled Lord Zheng, fathered Dangshi, Han Grand Minister of Agriculture, who lived at Kaifeng in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Duke You's son Lu was ancestor to Rong in the sixth generation, known as Lord Zheng; Rong's descendant Dangshi, Han Grand Minister of Agriculture, settled at Kaifeng in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 生韜，韜生江都守仲，仲生房，房生趙相季，季生議郎奇。

translations.literal: He fathered Tao; Tao fathered Zhong, Administrator of Jiangdu; Zhong fathered Fang; Fang fathered Ji, Chancellor of Zhao; Ji fathered Gentleman-advisor Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The line ran through Tao and Zhong, Administrator of Jiangdu, to Fang, then Ji, Chancellor of Zhao, and Gentleman-advisor Qi.

sentences.zh: 奇生穉，漢末自陳居河南開封，晉置滎陽郡，遂為郡人。

translations.literal: Qi fathered Zhi; at the end of Han he moved from Chen to Kaifeng in Henan; Jin established Xingyang commandery, and they became men of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's son Zhi left Chen for Kaifeng in Henan in the late Han; when Jin created Xingyang commandery, the family became its permanent residents.

sentences.zh: 穉生御史中丞賓，賓生興，字贛，蓮勺令。

translations.literal: Zhi fathered Imperial Secretary Bin; Bin fathered Xing, styled Gan, Magistrate of Lianzhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son Bin was father to Xing, styled Gan, Magistrate of Lianzhuo.

translations.literal: Xing fathered Zhong, styled Zhongshi, Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Xing's son Zhong, styled Zhongshi, served as Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 衆生城門校尉安世，安世生騎都尉綝，綝生上計掾熙，熙二子：泰、渾。

translations.literal: Zhong fathered Colonel of the City Gates Anshi; Anshi fathered Commandant of Cavalry Chen; Chen fathered Chief Clerk for Revenue Xi; Xi had two sons: Tai and Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's line continued through Anshi, Colonel of the City Gates, and Chen, Commandant of Cavalry, to Xi, Chief Clerk for Revenue, who had two sons: Tai and Hun.

translations.literal: Hun, Wei Vice Minister of the Palace Stores and Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Hun served Wei as Vice Minister of the Palace Stores and Master of Works.

translations.literal: Hun fathered Chong, Jin Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's son Chong was Jin Inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 崇生遹，遹生隨，扶風太守。

translations.literal: Chong fathered Sui; Sui fathered Sui, Administrator of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's line ran through Sui to another Sui, Administrator of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 隨生趙侍中略，略六子：翳、豁、淵、靜、悅、楚。

translations.literal: Sui fathered Lue, Attendant-in-Ordinary of Zhao; Lue had six sons: Yi, Huo, Yuan, Jing, Yue, and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator's descendant Lue, Attendant-in-Ordinary of Zhao, had six sons: Yi, Huo, Yuan, Jing, Yue, and Chu.

sentences.zh: 豁字君明，燕太子少傅、濟南公，生溫。

translations.literal: Huo, styled Junming, was Junior Tutor to the Heir of Yan and Duke of Jinan; he fathered Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Huo, styled Junming, served as Junior Tutor to the Heir of Yan and Duke of Jinan; his son was Wen.

translations.literal: Wen had four sons: Tao, Ye, Jian, and Tian.
translations.idiomatic: Wen had four sons: Tao, Ye, Jian, and Tian.

translations.literal: Tao lived in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's branch settled in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 曄，後魏建威將軍、南陽公，為北祖。

translations.literal: Ye, Northern Wei General Who Establishes Might and Duke of Nanyang, was the Northern Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, Northern Wei General Who Establishes Might and Duke of Nanyang, became the Northern Ancestor of the clan.

translations.literal: Jian was the Southern Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Jian founded the Southern Ancestor line.

translations.literal: Tian was the Central Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Tian founded the Central Ancestor line.

sentences.zh: 曄生中書博士茂，一名小白，七子：白麟、胤伯、叔夜、洞林、歸藏、連山、幼麟，因號「七房鄭氏」。

translations.literal: Ye fathered Mao, Doctor of the Secretariat, also called Little Bai; seven sons: Bailin, Yinbo, Shuye, Donglin, Guicang, Lianshan, and Youlin—hence styled the "Seven Houses of the Zheng clan."
translations.idiomatic: Ye's son Mao, a Doctor of the Secretariat also known as Little Bai, had seven sons—Bailin, Yinbo, Shuye, Donglin, Guicang, Lianshan, and Youlin—giving rise to the name "Seven Houses of the Zheng clan."

sentences.zh: 大房白麟後絕，第三房叔夜後無聞。

translations.literal: The senior house of Bailin died out; the third house of Shuye left no further record.
translations.idiomatic: Bailin's senior house died out, and Shuye's third house faded from record.

translations.literal: The Southern Ancestor Zheng clan:
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng clan of the Southern Ancestor line:

translations.literal: The Xingyang Zheng clan also had Zheng Shaolin.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Xingyang Zheng there was also Zheng Shaolin.

translations.literal: The Cangzhou Zheng clan:
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng clan of Cangzhou:

sentences.zh: 鄭氏定著二房：一曰北祖，二曰南祖。

translations.literal: The Zheng clan had two established houses: first the Northern Ancestor, second the Southern Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The Zheng were reckoned in two principal houses: the Northern Ancestor and the Southern Ancestor.

translations.literal: Nine chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: They produced nine chancellors.

sentences.zh: 北祖有珣瑜、覃、朗、餘慶、從讜、延昌；

translations.literal: The Northern Ancestor had Xunyu, Tan, Lang, Yuqing, Congdang, and Yanchang;
translations.idiomatic: From the Northern Ancestor came Xunyu, Tan, Lang, Yuqing, Congdang, and Yanchang;

translations.literal: the Southern Ancestor had Yin;
translations.idiomatic: from the Southern Ancestor came Yin;

translations.literal: the Xingyang Zheng had Tian;
translations.idiomatic: the Xingyang Zheng produced Tian;

translations.literal: the Cangzhou Zheng had Yin.
translations.idiomatic: and the Cangzhou Zheng produced Yin.

sentences.zh: 鍾鍾氏出自子姓，與宗氏皆晉伯宗之後也。

translations.literal: The Zhong clan—Zhong—came from the Zi surname; together with the Zong clan they were both descendants of Bo Zong of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhong clan traced its origin to the Zi line; both they and the Zong clan descended from Bo Zong of Jin.

sentences.zh: 伯宗子州犂仕楚，食采於鍾離，因以為姓。

translations.literal: Bo Zong's son Zili served Chu and received Zhongli as his fief; he took it as his surname.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Zong's son Zili entered Chu's service and took his fief at Zhongli as his surname.

sentences.zh: 楚漢時有鍾離眛，為項羽將，有二子：長曰發，居九江，仍故姓；

translations.literal: At the Chu–Han transition there was Zhongli Mo, a general of Xiang Yu; he had two sons: the elder called Fa, who lived in Jiujiang and kept the old surname;
translations.idiomatic: In the Chu–Han era Zhongli Mo served Xiang Yu as a general; his elder son Fa remained in Jiujiang and kept the Zhongli surname;

sentences.zh: 次曰接，居潁川長社，為鍾氏。

translations.literal: the younger called Jie, who lived in Changshe in Yingchuan and became the Zhong clan.
translations.idiomatic: his younger son Jie settled at Changshe in Yingchuan and founded the Zhong clan.

sentences.zh: 漢有西曹掾皓，字季明，二子：迪、敷。

translations.literal: In Han there was Western Bureau Clerk Hao, styled Jiming; two sons: Di and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han, Hao served as Western Bureau Clerk, styled Jiming, and had two sons: Di and Fu.

translations.literal: Di, Commandery Chief Clerk, fathered You and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Di, a Commandery Chief Clerk, fathered You and Yan.

sentences.zh: 繇字元常，魏太傅、定陵侯。

translations.literal: You, styled Yuanchang, was Wei Grand Tutor and Marquis of Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: You, styled Yuanchang, was Wei Grand Tutor and Marquis of Dingling.

translations.literal: He fathered Yu and Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Yu and Hui.

translations.literal: Yu, styled Zhishu, was Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Zhishu, served as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 生駿，駿字伯道，晉黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He fathered Jun; Jun, styled Bodao, was Jin Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son Jun, styled Bodao, was Jin Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

translations.literal: He fathered Ye, styled Shuguang, a clerk in the Ducal Office.
translations.idiomatic: Jun fathered Ye, styled Shuguang, a clerk in the Ducal Office.

sentences.zh: 生雅，字彥胄，過江仕晉，侍中。

translations.literal: He fathered Ya, styled Yanzhou, who crossed the river and served Jin as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's son Ya, styled Yanzhou, crossed the Yangtze to serve Jin as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

translations.literal: He fathered Dan, styled Shichang, Army Major of the Central Command.
translations.idiomatic: Ya fathered Dan, styled Shichang, Army Major of the Central Command.

translations.literal: He fathered Jing, styled Daoji, Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's son Jing, styled Daoji, was Administrator of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 生源，字循本，後魏永安太守。

translations.literal: He fathered Yuan, styled Xunben, Northern Wei Administrator of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jing fathered Yuan, styled Xunben, Northern Wei Administrator of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 生挺，字法秀，襄城太守、潁川郡公。

translations.literal: He fathered Ting, styled Faxiu, Administrator of Xiangcheng and Duke of Yingchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's son Ting, styled Faxiu, was Administrator of Xiangcheng and Duke of Yingchuan commandery.

translations.literal: He fathered Dao, styled Zhiyi, Central Army of Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Ting fathered Dao, styled Zhiyi, Central Army of Southern Qi.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yu and Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Dao had two sons: Yu and Rong.

translations.literal: Yu, styled Xiuwang, was Assistant Magistrate of Yongjia in Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Xiuwang, was Assistant Magistrate of Yongjia under Liang.

translations.literal: He fathered Chong, styled Yuanfu, who was Magistrate of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fathered Chong, styled Yuanfu, Magistrate of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 避侯景之難，徙居南康贛縣，生寶慎。

translations.literal: Fleeing the turmoil of Hou Jing, he moved to Gan county in Nankang and fathered Baoshen.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing Hou Jing's rebellion, he relocated to Gan county in Nankang and had a son Baoshen.

translations.literal: Of the Zhong clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhong clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Shaojing.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojing.

translations.literal: The Song clan—Song—came from the Zi surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Song clan traced its origin to the Zi surname.

sentences.zh: 殷王帝乙長子啟，周武王封之於宋，三十六世至君偃，為楚所滅，子孫以國為氏。

translations.literal: Qi, eldest son of Emperor Yi of Yin, was enfeoffed at Song by King Wu of Zhou; through thirty-six generations to Lord Yan it was destroyed by Chu, and the descendants took the state name as their clan.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, eldest son of Emperor Yi of the Yin, received Song from King Wu of Zhou; thirty-six generations later Lord Yan was destroyed by Chu, and his descendants took Song as their surname.

sentences.zh: 楚有上將軍義，義生昌，漢中尉，始居西河介休。

translations.literal: In Chu there was Senior General Yi; Yi fathered Chang, Han Commandant, who first settled at Jiexiu in Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: In Chu, Senior General Yi was ancestor to Chang, Han Commandant, who first settled the family at Jiexiu in Xihe.

sentences.zh: 十二世孫晃，晃三子：恭、畿、洽，徙廣平利人。

translations.literal: The twelfth-generation descendant Huang; Huang had three sons: Gong, Ji, and Qia, who moved to Liren in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve generations later came Huang, who had three sons—Gong, Ji, and Qia—who relocated to Liren in Guangping.

translations.literal: There was also the Guangping Song clan:
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Guangping branch of the Song clan:

translations.literal: Of the Song clan there were two chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The Song clan produced two chancellors.

translations.literal: Jing and Shenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Shenxi.

sentences.zh: 源源氏出自後魏聖武帝詰汾長子疋孤。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan—Yuan—came from Chidu, eldest son of Northern Wei Emperor Shenwu Jiefen.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan clan traced its origin to Chidu, eldest son of Northern Wei's Emperor Shenwu Jiefen.

sentences.zh: 七世孫禿髮傉檀，據南涼，子賀降後魏，太武見之曰：「與卿同源，可改為源氏。」

translations.literal: The seventh-generation descendant Tufa Rutan held Southern Liang; his son He surrendered to Northern Wei, and Emperor Taiwu seeing him said: "You and I share the same source—you may change to the Yuan clan."
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations later Tufa Rutan ruled Southern Liang; his son He submitted to Northern Wei, and Emperor Taiwu said, "We share the same origin—you may take the surname Yuan.

translations.literal: He held the rank of Grand Commandant and was Prince Xuan of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Commandant and Prince Xuan of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 生侍中馮翊惠公懷，懷二子：子邕、子恭。

translations.literal: He fathered Attendant-in-Ordinary Duke Hui of Fengyi Huai; Huai had two sons: Ziyong and Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huai, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Duke Hui of Fengyi, had two sons: Ziyong and Zigong.

sentences.zh: 子恭字靈順，中書監、臨汝文獻公，周、隋之際，居鄴郡安陽。

translations.literal: Zigong, styled Lingshun, was Director of the Secretariat and Duke Wenxian of Linru; in the Zhou–Sui transition the family lived at Anyang in Ye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong, styled Lingshun, served as Director of the Secretariat and Duke Wenxian of Linru; during the Zhou–Sui transition the family resided at Anyang in Ye commandery.

sentences.zh: 生彪，字文宗，隋莒州刺史、臨潁縣公，生師民。

translations.literal: He fathered Biao, styled Wenzong, Sui Inspector of Ju Prefecture and Duke of Linying county; Biao fathered Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, styled Wenzong, served Sui as Inspector of Ju and Duke of Linying; his son was Shimin.

translations.literal: Of the Yuan clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Qianyao.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao.

translations.literal: The Niu clan—Niu—came from the Zi surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Niu clan traced its origin to the Zi surname.

sentences.zh: 宋微子之後司寇牛父，子孫以王父字為氏。

translations.literal: After Song's Prince Wei, Minister of Crime Niu Fu; descendants took their grandfather's style-character as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of Song's Prince Wei took the style-name of Niu Fu, Minister of Crime, as their surname.

sentences.zh: 漢有牛邯，為護羌校尉，因居隴西，後徙安定，再徙鶉觚。

translations.literal: In Han there was Niu Han, who served as Protector of the Qiang; he settled in Longxi, later moved to Anding, and again to Chunggu.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Niu Han served as Protector of the Qiang and settled in Longxi, later moving to Anding and then Chunggu.

sentences.zh: 安定牛氏，出自漢隴西主簿崇之後。

translations.literal: The Anding Niu clan came from the descendants of Han Longxi Chief Clerk Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Anding branch of the Niu descended from Han Longxi Chief Clerk Chongzhi.

translations.literal: Of the Niu clan there were two chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The Niu clan produced two chancellors.

translations.literal: Xianke and Sengru.
translations.idiomatic: Xianke and Sengru.

translations.literal: The Miao clan—Miao—came from the Qian surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao clan traced its origin to the Qian surname.

sentences.zh: 楚若敖生鬬伯比，伯比生子良。

translations.literal: Chu's Ruoao fathered Dou Bobi; Bobi fathered Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's Lord Ruoao fathered Dou Bobi, whose son was Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 子良生越椒，字伯棼，以罪誅。

translations.literal: Ziliang fathered Yue Jiao, styled Bofen, who was executed for crime.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang's son Yue Jiao, styled Bofen, was put to death for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 其子賁皇奔晉，晉侯與之苗邑，因以為氏，其地河內軹縣南有苗亭，即其地也。

translations.literal: His son Benhuang fled to Jin; the Jin ruler granted him Miao as a fief, and he took it as his clan name—the place south of Zhi county in Henei had Miao pavilion, which was this territory.
translations.idiomatic: His son Benhuang fled to Jin and received the fief of Miao, which became the clan name—the old site lay south of Zhi county in Henei at Miao pavilion.

translations.literal: In Shangdang's Changzi county there was Miao Xi Kui.
translations.idiomatic: In Changzi county of Shangdang there was Miao Xi Kui.

translations.literal: Of the Miao clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Jinqing.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing.

translations.literal: The Lü clan—Lü—came from the Jiang surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Lü clan traced its origin to the Jiang surname.

sentences.zh: 炎帝裔孫為諸侯，號共工氏，有地在弘農之間，從孫伯夷，佐堯掌禮，使徧掌四岳，為諸侯伯，號太岳。

translations.literal: A descendant of the Flame Emperor became a feudal lord, styled the Gonggong clan, with territory between Hongnong; a collateral descendant Boyi assisted Yao in charge of ritual, was sent to oversee the Four Peaks, became chief among the feudal lords, and was styled Grand Yue.
translations.idiomatic: A Flame Emperor descendant ruled as Lord Gonggong in the Hongnong region; collateral descendant Boyi assisted Yao in ritual affairs, oversaw the Four Peaks as chief among feudal lords, and was called Grand Yue.

sentences.zh: 又佐禹治水，有功，賜氏曰呂，封為呂侯。

translations.literal: He also assisted Yu in controlling the waters, had merit, and was granted the clan name Lü and enfeoffed as Marquis of Lü.
translations.idiomatic: He also aided Yu in flood control and was granted the surname Lü and enfeoffment as Marquis of Lü.

sentences.zh: 呂者，膂也，謂能為股肱心膂也。

translations.literal: Lü means the loins—signifying ability to serve as arms, thighs, heart, and loins.
translations.idiomatic: Lü means "loins," denoting one who could serve as the ruler's supporting sinew and heart.

translations.literal: The territory was present-day Xin Cai in Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Their domain was present-day Xin Cai in Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷夏、商，世有國土，至周穆王，呂侯入為司寇，宣王世改「呂」為「甫」，春秋時為彊國所幷，其地後為蔡平侯所居。

translations.literal: Through Xia and Shang they held state territory; under King Mu of Zhou the Marquis of Lü entered service as Minister of Crime; in King Xuan's time "Lü" was changed to "Fu"; in Spring and Autumn a powerful state annexed them, and the land later became the residence of Marquis Ping of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: They held territory through Xia and Shang; under King Mu of Zhou the Lü marquis became Minister of Crime; King Xuan changed Lü to Fu; in Spring and Autumn a great power absorbed the state, and the land later belonged to Marquis Ping of Cai.

sentences.zh: 呂侯枝庶子孫，當商、周之際，或為庶人。

translations.literal: Collateral and lesser descendants of the Marquis of Lü, at the Shang–Zhou transition, sometimes became commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser branches of the Lü marquis line sometimes fell to commoner status in the Shang–Zhou transition.

sentences.zh: 呂尚字子牙，號太公望，封於齊。

translations.literal: Lü Shang, styled Ziya, titled Taigong Wang, was enfeoffed at Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shang, styled Ziya and known as Taigong Wang, received Qi as his fief.

sentences.zh: 十九世孫康公貸為田和所篡，遷於海濱。

translations.literal: The nineteenth-generation descendant Duke Kang Dai was usurped by Tian He and removed to the seashore.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth generation Duke Kang was displaced by Tian He and sent to live by the sea.

sentences.zh: 康公七世孫禮，秦昭襄王十九年自齊奔秦，為柱國、少宰、北平侯。

translations.literal: Duke Kang's seventh-generation descendant Li, in the nineteenth year of King Zhaoxiang of Qin fled Qi for Qin, serving as Pillar of State, Junior Minister, and Marquis of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations after Duke Kang, Li fled Qi for Qin in King Zhaoxiang's nineteenth year and became Pillar of State, Junior Minister, and Marquis of Beiping.

translations.literal: Two sons: Bochang and Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Li had two sons: Bochang and Zhongjing.

sentences.zh: 伯昌生青，以令尹從漢高祖，封陽信侯，謚曰胡。

translations.literal: Bochang fathered Qing, who as Chief Minister followed Emperor Gaozu of Han and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangxin, posthumously titled Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Bochang's son Qing followed Han Gaozu as Chief Minister and was enfeoffed Marquis of Yangxin with posthumous title Hu.

sentences.zh: 唐有隋州刺史仁宗，即其後也。

translations.literal: In Tang there was Sui Prefecture Inspector Renzong—his descendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang, Sui Prefecture Inspector Renzong descended from this line.

sentences.zh: 康公未失國時，呂氏子孫先已散居韓、魏、齊、魯之間，其後又徙東平壽張。

translations.literal: Before Duke Kang lost his state, Lü descendants had already scattered through Han, Wei, Qi, and Lu; later they moved to Shouzhang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Even before Duke Kang lost Qi, the Lü had scattered through Han, Wei, Qi, and Lu; later they relocated to Shouzhang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 魏有徐州刺史萬年亭侯虔，字子路，孫行鈞，其後世居河東。

translations.literal: In Wei there was Inspector of Xuzhou Qian, Marquis of Wannian Pavilion, styled Zilu; his grandson Xingjun—afterward the clan for generations lived in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had Xuzhou Inspector Qian, Marquis of Wannian Pavilion, styled Zilu; his grandson Xingjun's line settled in Hedong for generations.

translations.literal: Of the Lü clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Lü clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yin.

translations.literal: The Diwu clan—Diwu—came from the Gui surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Diwu clan traced its origin to the Gui surname.

sentences.zh: 齊諸田，漢初多徙奉園陵者，故以次第為氏。

translations.literal: The various Tian of Qi, many of whom in early Han were moved to serve the imperial park-tombs, therefore took ordinal numbers as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Many Qi Tian clansmen relocated in early Han to tend the imperial tombs and took ordinal numbers as surnames—hence Diwu, "Fifth."

translations.literal: In Tang there was Diwu Hua; his younger brother Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang were Diwu Hua and his younger brother Qi.

translations.literal: Of the Diwu clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Diwu clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi.

translations.literal: The Chang clan—Chang—came from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Chang clan traced its origin to the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 衞康叔支孫食采常邑，因以為氏。

translations.literal: A collateral descendant of Duke Kang of Wei received Chang as a fief and took it as his clan name.
translations.idiomatic: A collateral line of Duke Kang of Wei held the fief of Chang and adopted it as their surname.

translations.literal: In Tang there was the Xinfeng Chang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang there was a Xinfeng branch of the Chang clan.

translations.literal: Of the Chang clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Chang clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Gun.
translations.idiomatic: Gun.

sentences.zh: 喬喬氏出自姬姓，本橋氏也。

translations.literal: The Qiao clan—Qiao—came from the Ji surname; originally the Qiao (bridge) clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiao clan traced its origin to the Ji surname and was originally written with "wood" as the Bridge clan.

sentences.zh: 漢太尉玄六世孫勤，後魏平原內史，從孝武入關，居同州，生朗，朗生達，後周文帝命橋氏去「木」，義取高遠也。

translations.literal: Han Grand Commandant Xuan's sixth-generation descendant Qin, Northern Wei Interior Secretary of Pingyuan, followed Emperor Xiaowu through the pass into Guanzhong and lived in Tong Prefecture; he fathered Lang; Lang fathered Da; Emperor Wen of Northern Zhou ordered the Qiao clan to remove "wood," taking the meaning of loftiness and distance.
translations.idiomatic: Han Grand Commandant Xuan's sixth-generation descendant Qin, Northern Wei Interior Secretary of Pingyuan, followed Emperor Xiaowu into the pass and settled in Tong; his line ran through Lang to Da, when Northern Zhou's Emperor Wen ordered the clan to drop "wood" from Qiao for loftiness.

translations.literal: For generations they lived in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The family resided in Taiyuan for generations.

translations.literal: Of the Qiao clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiao clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Lin.

sentences.zh: 關關氏出自商大夫關龍逢之後。

translations.literal: The Guan clan—Guan—came from Shang minister Guan Longfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Guan clan descended from Shang minister Guan Longfeng.

sentences.zh: 蜀前將軍漢壽亭侯羽，生侍中興，其後世居信都。

translations.literal: Shu's Front General and Marquis of Hanshou Ting Yu fathered Attendant-in-Ordinary Xing; afterward the clan for generations lived in Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Front General and Marquis of Hanshou Ting, Guan Yu, had a son Xing, Attendant-in-Ordinary; later generations lived in Xindu.

translations.literal: Descendant Bo served as chancellor to Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: Descendant Bo served as chancellor to Emperor Dezong.

translations.literal: Of the Guan clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Guan clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Bo.

sentences.zh: 渾渾氏出自匈奴渾邪王，隨拓拔氏徙河南，因以為氏。

translations.literal: The Hun clan—Hun—came from the Xiongnu King Hunye, who followed the Tuoba and moved to Henan, taking it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: The Hun clan descended from Xiongnu King Hunye, who followed the Tuoba south to Henan and adopted Hun as their surname.

sentences.zh: 自迥貴至瑊，世襲皐蘭州都督。

translations.literal: From Jiong Gui to Jian they for generations inherited the post of Governor of Gaolan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiong Gui to Jian the family hereditarily held the governorship of Gaolan Prefecture.

translations.literal: Of the Hun clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Hun clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Jian.

translations.literal: The Qi clan—Qi—came from the Jiang surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi clan traced its origin to the Jiang surname.

sentences.zh: 炎帝裔孫呂尚後封於齊，因以為氏。

translations.literal: A descendant of the Flame Emperor, after Lü Shang was enfeoffed at Qi, took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of the Flame Emperor, after Lü Shang received Qi, took Qi as their surname.

sentences.zh: 漢有平敬侯齊受，傳封四世，居高陽。

translations.literal: In Han there was Marquis of Pingjing Qi Shou; the enfeoffment passed four generations; they lived in Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Qi Shou was Marquis of Pingjing; the title passed four generations while the clan lived in Gaoyang.

translations.literal: In Jin there was Marquis of Wuyi Qi Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin, Qi Yan was Marquis of Wuyi.

translations.literal: The Qi clan of Ying Prefecture
translations.idiomatic: The Qi clan of Ying Prefecture:

translations.literal: Of the Qi clan there were two chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi clan produced two chancellors.

translations.literal: Kang and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Kang and Ying.

translations.literal: The Dong clan—Dong—came from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Dong clan traced its origin to the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 黃帝裔孫有飂叔安，生董父，舜賜姓董氏。

translations.literal: A descendant of the Yellow Emperor had Liaoshu An, who fathered Dong Fu; Shun granted the clan name Dong.
translations.idiomatic: A Yellow Emperor descendant, Liaoshu An, fathered Dong Fu; Shun granted the surname Dong.

sentences.zh: 裔孫辛有，辛有子孫分適晉，有董孤。

translations.literal: Descendant Xin You; Xin You's descendants dispersed to Jin, among whom was Dong Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Descendant Xin You's line split into Jin, producing Dong Hu.

sentences.zh: 裔孫翳，項羽封為翟王，都高奴，子孫遂居隴西。

translations.literal: Descendant Yi; Xiang Yu enfeoffed him as King of Di, with his capital at Gaonu; descendants then lived in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Descendant Yi was made King of Di by Xiang Yu, capital at Gaonu; his descendants settled in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 漢江都相仲舒少子之孫，自廣川徙隴西，裔孫徙河東。

translations.literal: Grandson of the younger son of Han Chancellor of Jiangdu Dong Zhongshu moved from Guangchuan to Longxi; a descendant moved to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: A grandson of Dong Zhongshu's younger son left Guangchuan for Longxi; later descendants moved to Hedong.

translations.literal: Of the Dong clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Dong clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin.

translations.literal: The Jia clan—Jia—came from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Jia clan traced its origin to the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 唐叔虞少子公明，康王封之於賈，為賈伯，河東臨汾有賈鄉，即其地也，為晉所滅，以國為氏。

translations.literal: Younger son of Tang Shuyu, Gongming, was enfeoffed at Jia by King Kang as Earl of Jia; Hedong Linfen had Jia township—this was the place; Jin destroyed it, and they took the state name as their clan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shuyu of Tang's younger son Gongming received Jia from King Kang as Earl of Jia; the site lay in Jia township near Linfen in Hedong; Jin destroyed the state and the clan took Jia as their surname.

sentences.zh: 晉公族狐偃之子射姑為晉太師，食邑於賈，字季他，亦號賈季。

translations.literal: Jin ducal clansman Hu Yan's son Shegu served Jin as Grand Master, with a fief at Jia, styled Jita, also called Jia Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Jin noble Hu Yan's son Shegu was Jin Grand Master with a fief at Jia, styled Jita, also known as Jia Ji.

sentences.zh: 漢有長沙王太傅誼，生璠，尚書中兵郎。

translations.literal: In Han there was Grand Tutor to the King of Changsha Yi; he fathered Fan, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing for Central Troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Jia Yi, Grand Tutor to the King of Changsha, fathered Fan, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing for Central Troops.

translations.literal: He fathered two sons: Jia and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Fan had two sons: Jia and Yun.

sentences.zh: 嘉，宜春太守，生敻，游擊將軍。

translations.literal: Jia, Administrator of Yichun, fathered Xiong, General of Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Jia, Administrator of Yichun, fathered Xiong, General of Rapid Cavalry.

translations.literal: Five sons: Hong, Run, Rui, Xiang, and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong had five sons: Hong, Run, Rui, Xiang, and Zhu.

sentences.zh: 汭，輕騎將軍，生曄，下邳太守。

translations.literal: Rui, General of Light Cavalry, fathered Ye, Administrator of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, General of Light Cavalry, fathered Ye, Administrator of Xiapi.

translations.literal: Two sons: Bing and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had two sons: Bing and Yuan.

translations.literal: Yuan, Administrator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was Administrator of Liaodong.

translations.literal: Three sons: Na, Bin, and Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had three sons: Na, Bin, and Pi.

translations.literal: Pi fathered Yi, Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Pi fathered Yi, Director of the Secretariat.

translations.literal: Two sons: Tingyu and Xiuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had two sons: Tingyu and Xiuyu.

sentences.zh: 秀玉，武威太守，生衍，兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Xiuyu, Administrator of Wuwei, fathered Yan, Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyu, Administrator of Wuwei, fathered Yan, Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 生龔，輕騎將軍，徙居武威。

translations.literal: He fathered Gong, General of Light Cavalry, who moved to live in Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Yan fathered Gong, General of Light Cavalry, who relocated to Wuwei.

translations.literal: Two sons: Cai and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had two sons: Cai and Xu.

sentences.zh: 詡，魏太尉、肅侯，生璣，駙馬都尉、關內侯，又徙長樂。

translations.literal: Xu, Wei Grand Commandant and Marquis Su, fathered Ji, Commandant of Horse for the Emperor's Sons-in-Law and Marquis Within the Passes; again they moved to Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, Wei Grand Commandant and Marquis Su, fathered Ji, Commandant of Horse for the Emperor's Sons-in-Law and Marquis Within the Passes; the line then moved to Changle.

translations.literal: Two sons: Tong and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had two sons: Tong and Yan.

translations.literal: Tong, Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Chariots and Cavalry.

translations.literal: Three sons: Zhong'an, Zhongmou, and Zhongda.
translations.idiomatic: Tong had three sons: Zhong'an, Zhongmou, and Zhongda.

translations.literal: Zhongda, Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongda was Administrator of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 生疋，字彥度，輕車將軍、雍州刺史、酒泉郡公。

translations.literal: He fathered Pi, styled Yandu, General of Light Chariots, Inspector of Yong Province, and Duke of Jiuquan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongda fathered Pi, styled Yandu, General of Light Chariots, Inspector of Yong Province, and Duke of Jiuquan commandery.

translations.literal: Two sons: Yi and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Pi had two sons: Yi and Kang.

translations.literal: Kang, Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was Director of the Secretariat.

translations.literal: Two sons: Kai and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Kang had two sons: Kai and Jun.

translations.literal: Jun fathered Bi, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Jun fathered Bi, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

translations.literal: Two sons: Gongzhi and Feizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Bi had two sons: Gongzhi and Feizhi.

translations.literal: Gongzhi, Army Major of the Song Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi was Army Major under the Song Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 四子：希鏡、希遠、希逸、希叟。

translations.literal: Four sons: Xijing, Xiyuan, Xiyi, and Xisou.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhi had four sons: Xijing, Xiyuan, Xiyi, and Xisou.

sentences.zh: 希鏡，南齊外兵郎，生梲，義興郡太守。

translations.literal: Xijing, Southern Qi Master of External Troops, fathered Tong, Administrator of Yixing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing, Southern Qi Master of External Troops, fathered Tong, Administrator of Yixing.

translations.literal: He fathered Zhi, Grand Steward of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He fathered Zhi, Grand Steward of Liang.

translations.literal: Two sons: Xian and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had two sons: Xian and Zhao.

translations.literal: Zhao had two sons: Huan and Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had two sons: Huan and Hong.

translations.literal: Hong, Later Liang Army Major of the Central Command.
translations.idiomatic: Hong served Later Liang as Army Major of the Central Command.

sentences.zh: 生勰，北齊青兗等州刺史、河東公。

translations.literal: He fathered Xie, Northern Qi Inspector of Qing, Yan, and other provinces and Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He fathered Xie, Northern Qi Inspector of Qing and Yan provinces and Duke of Hedong.

translations.literal: Two sons: Min and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie had two sons: Min and Yan.

translations.literal: Yan, Supervisor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Supervisor of the Palace.

translations.literal: Three sons: Yi, Que, and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had three sons: Yi, Que, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲避葛榮之難，避地浮陽。

translations.literal: Xian, fleeing the turmoil of Ge Rong, took refuge in Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xian fled Ge Rong's rebellion and took refuge in Fuyang.

translations.literal: Of the Jia clan there were two chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The Jia clan produced two chancellors.

translations.literal: Dan and Su.
translations.idiomatic: Dan and Su.

translations.literal: The Quan clan—Quan—came from the Zi surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Quan clan traced its origin to the Zi surname.

sentences.zh: 商武丁之裔孫封於權，其地南郡當陽縣權城是也。

translations.literal: A descendant of Shang's King Wuding was enfeoffed at Quan; the place was Quan city in Dangyang county, Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of King Wuding of Shang was enfeoffed at Quan—present-day Quan city in Dangyang, Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 楚武王滅權，遷於那處，其孫因以為氏。

translations.literal: King Wu of Chu destroyed Quan and moved the people to Na; his descendants took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu of Chu destroyed Quan and relocated the clan to Na, his descendants took Quan as their surname.

sentences.zh: 秦滅楚，遷大姓於隴西，因居天水。

translations.literal: Qin destroyed Chu and moved great clans to Longxi; they settled in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin destroyed Chu, great families were moved to Longxi and settled in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 漢有左輔都尉忠，十四世孫翼，字子良，前秦右僕射、安丘敬公。

translations.literal: In Han there was Left Assistant Commandant Zhong; the fourteenth-generation descendant Yi, styled Ziliang, was Former Qin Right Vice Director and Duke Jing of Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Left Assistant Commandant Zhong was ancestor to Yi, styled Ziliang, Former Qin Right Vice Director and Duke Jing of Anqiu, fourteen generations later.

translations.literal: He fathered Xuanji and Xuanbao.
translations.idiomatic: Yi fathered Xuanji and Xuanbao.

sentences.zh: 宣褒，後秦黃門侍郎，六世孫榮。

translations.literal: Xuanbao, Later Qin Gentleman at the Yellow Gate; sixth-generation descendant Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbao, Later Qin Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, was ancestor to Rong in the sixth generation.

translations.literal: Of the Quan clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Quan clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Deyu.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu.

translations.literal: The Huangfu clan—Huangfu—came from the Zi surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangfu clan traced its origin to the Zi surname.

sentences.zh: 宋戴公白生公子充石，字皇父。

translations.literal: Duke Dai of Song, Bai, fathered the lord's son Chongshi, styled Huangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Dai of Song, Bai, fathered the lord's son Chongshi, styled Huangfu.

sentences.zh: 皇父生季子來，來生南雍𡙇，以王父字為氏。

translations.literal: Huangfu fathered the youngest son Lai; Lai fathered Nanyong Kui; they took their grandfather's style-character as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu's youngest son Lai fathered Nanyong Kui; the line took their grandfather's style-name Huangfu as their surname.

sentences.zh: 𡙇六世孫孟之，孟之生遇，避地奔魯。

translations.literal: Kui's sixth-generation descendant Mengzhi; Mengzhi fathered Yu, who fled and went to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations after Kui came Mengzhi, whose son Yu fled to Lu.

sentences.zh: 裔孫鸞，漢興，自魯徙茂陵，改「父」為「甫」。

translations.literal: Descendant Luan; at Han's rise he moved from Lu to Maoling and changed the character for "father" to "Fu."
translations.idiomatic: Descendant Luan, at the founding of Han, moved from Lu to Maoling and changed the surname character from "father" to "Fu."

sentences.zh: 裔孫晉廣魏太守固，生柴，徙襄陽，後又徙壽春，裔孫珍義。

translations.literal: Descendant Gu, Jin Administrator of Guangling in Wei, fathered Chai, who moved to Xiangyang and later to Shouchun; descendant Zhenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Descendant Gu, Jin Administrator of Guangling in Wei, fathered Chai, who moved to Xiangyang and later Shouchun; later came Zhenyi.

translations.literal: Of the Huangfu clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangfu clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Bo.

translations.literal: The Cheng clan—Cheng—came from the Feng surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Cheng clan traced its origin to the Feng surname.

translations.literal: Zhuanxu fathered Cheng; Cheng fathered Laotong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuanxu fathered Cheng, who fathered Laotong.

translations.literal: Laotong had two sons: Chong and Li.
translations.idiomatic: Laotong had two sons: Chong and Li.

sentences.zh: 重為火正，司地，其後世為掌天地之官。

translations.literal: Chong was Director of Fire and oversaw the earth; his descendants for generations were officials in charge of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Chong became Director of Fire and oversaw the earth; his descendants for generations held offices regulating Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 裔孫封於程，是謂程伯，雒陽有上程聚，即其地也。

translations.literal: A descendant was enfeoffed at Cheng—called Earl of Cheng; Luoyang had Shangcheng cluster, which was this place.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant was enfeoffed at Cheng as Earl of Cheng; Luoyang's Shangcheng cluster marked the old site.

sentences.zh: 至周宣王時，程伯休父失其官守，以諸侯入為王司馬，又有司馬氏。

translations.literal: By King Xuan of Zhou, Earl of Cheng Xiufu lost his office and fief and entered as King's Minister of War; there was also the Sima clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Xuan of Zhou, Earl of Cheng Xiufu lost office and entered court as Royal Minister of War, founding also the Sima clan.

translations.literal: The Cheng clan for generations lived in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Cheng clan resided in Chang'an for generations.

translations.literal: Of the Cheng clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Cheng clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi.

translations.literal: The Linghu clan—Linghu—came from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Linghu clan traced its origin to the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 周文王子畢公高裔孫畢萬，為晉大夫，生芒季。

translations.literal: Duke Gao of Bi, descendant of King Wen of Zhou's son, Bi Wan served Jin as grandee and fathered Mangji.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Wan, descendant of King Wen's son Duke Gao of Bi, was a Jin grandee and fathered Mangji.

translations.literal: Mangji fathered Wu Zi Wei Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Mangji fathered Wu Zi Wei Chu.

sentences.zh: 犫生顆，以獲秦將杜回功，別封令狐，生文子頡，因以為氏，世居太原。

translations.literal: Chu fathered Kui; for capturing Qin general Du Hui he was separately enfeoffed at Linghu and fathered Wenzi Jie; he took it as his clan name; for generations they lived in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu's son Kui, enfeoffed separately at Linghu for capturing Qin general Du Hui, fathered Wenzi Jie, who took Linghu as the surname; the clan lived in Taiyuan for generations.

sentences.zh: 秦有太原守五馬亭侯範，十四世孫漢建威將軍邁，與翟義起兵討王莽，兵敗死之。

translations.literal: In Qin there was Administrator of Taiyuan Fan, Marquis of Wuma Pavilion; fourteenth-generation descendant Han General Who Establishes Might Mai, who with Zhai Yi raised troops against Wang Mang and died when defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Qin had Taiyuan Administrator Fan, Marquis of Wuma Pavilion; fourteen generations later Mai, Han General Who Establishes Might, died fighting Wang Mang alongside Zhai Yi.

sentences.zh: 三子：伯友、文公、稱，皆奔燉煌。

translations.literal: Three sons: Boyou, Wengong, and Cheng—all fled to Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Mai had three sons—Boyou, Wengong, and Cheng—who all fled to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 伯友入龜茲，文公入疏勒，稱為故吏所匿，遂居効轂。

translations.literal: Boyou entered Kucha, Wengong entered Shule, and Cheng was hidden by a former clerk and thus lived at Xiaogu.
translations.idiomatic: Boyou reached Kucha, Wengong Shule, and Cheng, hidden by a former clerk, settled at Xiaogu.

translations.literal: Cheng had six sons: Fu, Jian, You, Xian, Jin, and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had six sons: Fu, Jian, You, Xian, Jin, and Meng.

sentences.zh: 由字仲平，後漢伊吾都尉。

translations.literal: You, styled Zhongping, was Later Han Commandant of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: You, styled Zhongping, was Later Han Commandant of Yiwu.

translations.literal: Six sons: Yu, Ba, Rong, Ming, Huan, and Chun.
translations.idiomatic: You had six sons: Yu, Ba, Rong, Ming, Huan, and Chun.

translations.literal: Yu, styled Juxian, was Administrator of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Juxian, was Administrator of Boling.

translations.literal: Four sons: Hui, Qia, Yan, and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had four sons: Hui, Qia, Yan, and Pu.

translations.literal: Pu, styled Wenwu, was Administrator of Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, styled Wenwu, was Administrator of Cangwu.

translations.literal: Three sons: Huang, Rui, and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Pu had three sons: Huang, Rui, and Yang.

sentences.zh: 溥五世孫晉諫議大夫馨，馨孫亞，字就胤，前涼西海太守、安人亭侯。

translations.literal: Pu's fifth-generation descendant Jin Remonstrating and Consulting Grandee Xin; Xin's grandson Ya, styled Jiuyin, was Former Liang Administrator of Xihai and Marquis of Anren Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations after Pu came Jin Remonstrating and Consulting Grandee Xin; his grandson Ya, styled Jiuyin, was Former Liang Administrator of Xihai and Marquis of Anren Pavilion.

translations.literal: Two sons: Ruan and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Ya had two sons: Ruan and Sui.

sentences.zh: 亞孫敏，字永昌，前涼鳴沙令。

translations.literal: Ya's grandson Min, styled Yongchang, was Former Liang Magistrate of Mingsha.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's grandson Min, styled Yongchang, was Former Liang Magistrate of Mingsha.

translations.literal: Four sons: Da, Zhong, Xi, and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Min had four sons: Da, Zhong, Xi, and Yue.

sentences.zh: 敏五世孫虬，字惠獻，後魏燉煌郡太守、鸇陰縣子。

translations.literal: Min's fifth-generation descendant Qiu, styled Huixian, was Later Wei Administrator of Dunhuang commandery and Viscount of Zhuanyin county.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations after Min came Qiu, styled Huixian, Later Wei Administrator of Dunhuang and Viscount of Zhuanyin.

translations.literal: Four sons: Yuanbao, Zheng, Qingbao, and Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had four sons: Yuanbao, Zheng, Qingbao, and Xiu.

sentences.zh: 整，周御正中大夫、彭陽襄公，賜姓宇文氏，生熙。

translations.literal: Zheng, Zhou Director of the Imperial Household and Duke Xiang of Pengyang, was granted the surname Yuwen and fathered Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, Zhou Director of the Imperial Household and Duke Xiang of Pengyang, received the surname Yuwen and fathered Xi.

translations.literal: Of the Linghu clan there were two chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The Linghu clan produced two chancellors.

translations.literal: Chu and Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and Tao.

translations.literal: The Duan clan—Duan—came from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Duan clan traced its origin to the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 鄭武公子共叔段，其孫以王父字為氏。

translations.literal: Duke Wu of Zheng's son Gongshu Duan—his descendants took their grandfather's style-character as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of Duke Wu of Zheng's son Gongshu Duan took their grandfather's style-name as their surname.

sentences.zh: 漢有北地都尉卬，世居武威。

translations.literal: In Han there was Beidi Commandant Ang; for generations they lived in Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Beidi Commandant Ang settled the clan in Wuwei for generations.

sentences.zh: 十四世孫後魏晉興太守紛。

translations.literal: Fourteenth-generation descendant Later Wei Administrator of Jinxing Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen generations later came Fen, Later Wei Administrator of Jinxing.

translations.literal: Fifth-generation descendant Yanshi moved to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations after Fen, Yanshi relocated the line to Henan.

translations.literal: Of the Duan clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Duan clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Wenchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang.

translations.literal: The Yuan clan—Yuan—came from the Tuoba clan.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial Yuan clan traced its origin to the Tuoba.

sentences.zh: 黃帝生昌意，昌意少子悃，居北，十一世為鮮卑君長。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor fathered Changyi; Changyi's younger son Kun lived in the north; in the eleventh generation he was chieftain of the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor fathered Changyi; Changyi's younger son Kun lived in the north, and in the eleventh generation his line became Xianbei chieftains.

sentences.zh: 平文皇帝鬱律二子：什翼犍、烏孤。

translations.literal: Emperor Pingwen Yulü had two sons: Shiyijian and Wugu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Pingwen Yulü had two sons: Shiyijian and Wugu.

sentences.zh: 什翼犍，昭成皇帝也，始號代王，至道武皇帝改號魏，至孝文帝更為元氏。

translations.literal: Shiyijian was Emperor Zhaocheng; he first styled himself King of Dai; under Emperor Daowu the title changed to Wei; under Emperor Xiaowen it became the Yuan clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyijian was Emperor Zhaocheng, first King of Dai; Emperor Daowu changed the state to Wei; Emperor Xiaowen adopted the surname Yuan.

sentences.zh: 什翼犍七子：一曰寔君，二曰翰，三曰閼婆，四曰壽鳩，五曰紇根，六曰力真，七曰窟咄。

translations.literal: Shiyijian had seven sons: first Shijun, second Han, third Kebopo, fourth Shoujiu, fifth Heggen, sixth Lizhen, seventh Kuzhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyijian had seven sons: Shijun, Han, Kebopo, Shoujiu, Heggen, Lizhen, and Kuzhuo.

sentences.zh: 寔君生道武皇帝珪，珪生明元皇帝嗣，嗣生太武皇帝燾，燾生景穆皇帝晃。

translations.literal: Shijun fathered Emperor Daowu Gui; Gui fathered Emperor Mingyuan Si; Si fathered Emperor Taiwu Tao; Tao fathered Emperor Jingmu Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Shijun fathered Emperor Daowu Gui; Gui fathered Mingyuan; Mingyuan fathered Taiwu; Taiwu fathered Jingmu.

sentences.zh: 景穆諸子唯濬、新成、子推、天錫、雲、禎、胡兒、休八房子孫聞於唐。

translations.literal: Of Jingmu's sons only Jun, Xincheng, Zitui, Tiansi, Yun, Zhen, Hu'er, and Xiu's eight houses' descendants were known in Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Of Emperor Jingmu's sons, only the eight houses of Jun, Xincheng, Zitui, Tiansi, Yun, Zhen, Hu'er, and Xiu left lines known in Tang.

translations.literal: Jun was Emperor Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was Emperor Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 文成諸子唯弘、長樂二房子孫聞於唐。

translations.literal: Of Wencheng's sons only Hong and Changle two houses' descendants were known in Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Of Emperor Wencheng's sons, only the Hong and Changle branches were known in Tang.

translations.literal: Hong was Emperor Xianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was Emperor Xianwen.

sentences.zh: 獻文諸子唯宏、幹、羽、勰四房子孫聞於唐。

translations.literal: Of Xianwen's sons only Hong, Gan, Yu, and Xie four houses' descendants were known in Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Of Emperor Xianwen's sons, only the Hong, Gan, Yu, and Xie branches were known in Tang.

translations.literal: Hong was Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was Emperor Xiaowen.

translations.literal: Seven sons: Xun, Ke, Huai, Yu, Yi, Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons: Xun, Ke, Huai, Yu, Yi, and Yue.

translations.literal: Ke was Emperor Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was Emperor Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 懷，廣平文穆王，生廣平文懿王悌，悌生侍中、驃騎大將軍、廣平王贊，贊生謙。

translations.literal: Huai, Prince Wenmu of Guangping, fathered Prince Wenyi of Guangping Ti; Ti fathered Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of Agile Cavalry, and Prince of Guangping Zan; Zan fathered Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Huai, Prince Wenmu of Guangping, fathered Ti, Prince Wenyi of Guangping; Ti fathered Zan, Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Agile Cavalry; Zan fathered Qian.

sentences.zh: 什翼犍第六子力真，力真二子：意烈、意勁。

translations.literal: Shiyijian's sixth son Lizhen; Lizhen had two sons: Yilie and Yijin.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyijian's sixth son Lizhen had two sons: Yilie and Yijin.

translations.literal: Yijin, Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yijin was Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 五世孫敷州刺史禎，禎二子：巖、成。

translations.literal: Fifth-generation descendant Inspector of Fuzhou Zhen; Zhen had two sons: Yan and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations later, Fuzhou Inspector Zhen had two sons: Yan and Cheng.

translations.literal: Of the Yuan clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen.

sentences.zh: 大曆宰相元載，本景氏，故不著。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yuan Zai of the Dali era was originally of the Jing clan and is therefore not listed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai, chancellor in the Dali era, was originally of the Jing clan and is therefore omitted.

translations.literal: The Lu clan—Lu—came from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu clan traced its origin to the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 帝摯子玄元，堯封於中路，歷虞、夏稱侯，子孫以國為氏。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhi's son Xuanyuan; Yao enfeoffed him at Zhonglu; through Yu and Xia he was styled marquis; descendants took the state name as their clan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhi's son Xuanyuan received Zhonglu from Yao; through Yu and Xia the line held marquis rank, and descendants took Lu as their surname.

sentences.zh: 漢符離侯博德始居平陽。

translations.literal: Han Marquis of Fuli Bode first settled in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Marquis of Fuli Bode first settled in Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 裔孫嘉，字君賓，晉安東太守。

translations.literal: Descendant Jia, styled Junbin, was Jin Administrator of Andong.
translations.idiomatic: Descendant Jia, styled Junbin, was Jin Administrator of Andong.

translations.literal: Grandson Zao; Zao had two sons Zuan and Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zao had two sons: Zuan and Jian.

sentences.zh: 又有越王府東閣史祭酒節，生惟恕。

translations.literal: There was also Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Prince of Yue's mansion Jie, who fathered Weishu.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Libationer Jie of the Prince of Yue's Eastern Pavilion, who fathered Weishu.

translations.literal: Of the Lu clan there were two chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu clan produced two chancellors.

translations.literal: Yan and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Sui.

translations.literal: The Shu clan—Shu—came from the Yan surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu clan traced its origin to the Yan surname.

sentences.zh: 皐陶之後封於蓼，安豐蓼縣即其地也。

translations.literal: After Gaoyao his descendants were enfeoffed at Liao; Anfeng Liao county was this place.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaoyao, descendants were enfeoffed at Liao—present-day Liao county in Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 春秋魯文公五年，為楚所滅，其後更復為楚屬國，亦名曰舒，又曰羣舒，又曰舒蓼，又曰舒庸，又曰舒鳩，一國而有五名。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Duke Wen of Lu in Spring and Autumn it was destroyed by Chu; afterward it again became a Chu dependency, also called Shu, also called the Group of Shu, also Shu-Liao, also Shu-Yong, also Shu-Jiu—one state with five names.
translations.idiomatic: In Lu Duke Wen's fifth year Chu destroyed it; it later became a Chu dependency known as Shu, the Group of Shu, Shu-Liao, Shu-Yong, and Shu-Jiu—one polity with five names.

sentences.zh: 春秋魯襄二十五年，楚又滅之，子孫以國為氏，世居廬江。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Duke Xiang of Lu in Spring and Autumn Chu again destroyed it; descendants took the state name as their clan and for generations lived in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Xiang of Lu's twenty-fifth year Chu destroyed the state again; descendants took Shu as their surname and settled in Lujiang for generations.

translations.literal: Of the Shu clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Yuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu.

translations.literal: The Bai clan—Bai—came from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Bai clan traced its origin to the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 周太王五世孫虞仲封於虞，為晉所滅。

translations.literal: Yu Zhong, fifth-generation descendant of Great King Tai of Zhou, was enfeoffed at Yu and was destroyed by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhong, fifth-generation descendant of Zhou's Great King Tai, was enfeoffed at Yu until Jin destroyed the state.

sentences.zh: 虞之公族井伯奚媵伯姬于秦，受邑於百里，因號百里奚。

translations.literal: Yu ducal clansman Jing Bo Xi accompanied Bo Ji to Qin as a secondary wife's escort, received a fief at Baili, and was therefore styled Baili Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu noble Jing Bo Xi went to Qin with Bo Ji as escort, received territory at Baili, and was known as Baili Xi.

sentences.zh: 奚生視，字孟明，古人皆先字後名，故稱為孟明視。

translations.literal: Xi fathered Shi, styled Mengming; ancients placed the style before the given name, hence he was called Mengming Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi fathered Shi, styled Mengming—in ancient usage the style preceded the name, hence Mengming Shi.

sentences.zh: 孟明視二子：一曰西乞術，二曰白乞丙，其後以為氏。

translations.literal: Mengming Shi had two sons: first Xiji Shu, second Baiqi Bing; afterward they took this as their clan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengming Shi had two sons, Xiji Shu and Baiqi Bing, whose descendants took Bai as their surname.

sentences.zh: 裔孫武安君起，賜死杜郵，始皇思其功，封其子仲於太原，故子孫世為太原人。

translations.literal: Descendant Lord Wu'an Qi was ordered to die at Duyou; the First Emperor mindful of his merit enfeoffed his son Zhong at Taiyuan, so descendants for generations were men of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Descendant Lord Wu'an Qi died by command at Duyou; Qin Shihuang enfeoffed his son Zhong at Taiyuan, and the clan remained there for generations.

sentences.zh: 二十三世孫後魏太原太守邕，邕五世孫建。

translations.literal: The twenty-third-generation descendant Later Wei Administrator of Taiyuan Yong; Yong's fifth-generation descendant Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-three generations later came Yong, Later Wei Administrator of Taiyuan; five generations after Yong came Jian.

translations.literal: Of the Bai clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Bai clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Minzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong.

translations.literal: The Xiahou clan—Xiahou—came from the Si surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiahou clan traced its origin to the Si surname.

sentences.zh: 夏禹裔孫東樓公封為𣏌侯，至簡公為楚所滅，弟他奔魯，魯悼公以其夏禹之後，給以采地為侯，因以為氏焉。

translations.literal: Xia Yu's descendant Duke Donglou was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qi; to Duke Jian it was destroyed by Chu; his younger brother Tuo fled to Lu; Duke Dao of Lu, because he was Xia Yu's descendant, granted him a fief as marquis, and he took it as his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu of Xia's descendant Duke Donglou was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qi; when Duke Jian was destroyed by Chu, his brother Tuo fled to Lu; Duke Dao of Lu, honoring him as Yu's descendant, granted a fief and the clan took Xiahou as their name.

sentences.zh: 後去魯之沛，分沛為譙，遂為郡人。

translations.literal: Later they left Lu's Pei; Pei was divided to form Qiao, and they became men of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later they left Pei in Lu; when Pei was split to form Qiao commandery, they became its residents.

translations.literal: In Tang there was Director of the Imperial Carriage Shenfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang, Shenfeng served as Director of the Imperial Carriage.

translations.literal: Of the Xiahou clan there was one chancellor.

translations.literal: He fathered Song Marquis of Chongsheng Xian; Xian fathered Later Wei Grandee of Chongsheng Cheng; Cheng fathered Secretariat Gentleman Lingzhen; Lingzhen fathered Wentai.
translations.idiomatic: The line produced Song Marquis of Chongsheng Xian, Later Wei Grandee of Chongsheng Cheng, Secretariat Gentleman Lingzhen, and Wentai.

translations.literal: From Lingzhen below they inherited Marquis of Chongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: From Lingzhen the Chongsheng marquisate passed for generations.

translations.literal: Wentai fathered Qu.
translations.idiomatic: Wentai fathered Qu.

sentences.zh: 下博孔氏出自關內侯福七世孫郁，後漢冀州刺史。

translations.literal: The Xiabo Kong clan came from Marquis Within the Passes Fu's seventh-generation descendant Yu, Later Han Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiabo Kong branch descended from Fu's seventh-generation descendant Yu, Later Han Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 生揚，下博亭侯，子孫因居焉。

translations.literal: He fathered Yang, Marquis of Xiabo; descendants therefore settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fathered Yang, Marquis of Xiabo, and descendants settled there.

sentences.zh: 七世孫靈龜，後魏國子博士。

translations.literal: Seventh-generation descendant Linggui, Later Wei Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Seven generations later came Linggui, Later Wei Erudite of the Imperial University.

translations.literal: He fathered Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Linggui fathered Shuo.

sentences.zh: 曲阜憲公穎達族孫務本。

translations.literal: Qufu Duke Xian Gong Yingda's collateral clansman Wuben.
translations.idiomatic: Wuben was a collateral kinsman of Duke Xian of Qufu, Yingda.

translations.literal: From Confucius to this point was thirty-five generations.
translations.idiomatic: From Confucius to this point was thirty-five generations.

translations.literal: Of the Kong clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Kong clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei.

translations.literal: The Dugu clan—Dugu—came from the Liu clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Dugu clan traced its origin to the Liu line.

sentences.zh: 後漢世祖生沛獻王輔，輔生釐王定，定生節王丐。

translations.literal: Later Han's Emperor Guangwu fathered Prince Xian of Pei Fu; Fu fathered Prince Li Ding; Ding fathered Prince Jie Gai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu fathered Prince Xian of Pei Fu; Fu fathered Prince Li Ding; Ding fathered Prince Jie Gai.

translations.literal: Gai had two sons: Guang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Gai had two sons: Guang and Yi.

translations.literal: Yi, Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was Magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 生穆，穆生度遼將軍進伯，擊匈奴，兵敗被執，囚之孤山下。

translations.literal: He fathered Mu; Mu fathered General Who Pacifies the Liao Jinbo; attacking the Xiongnu he was defeated and captured, imprisoned beneath Gushan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi fathered Mu; Mu fathered Jinbo, General Who Pacifies the Liao; defeated by the Xiongnu, he was captured and held beneath Gushan.

sentences.zh: 生尸利，單于以為谷蠡王，號獨孤部。

translations.literal: He fathered Shili; the Chanyu made him King of the Left Valley, styled the Dugu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: He fathered Shili; the Chanyu made him King of the Left Valley and styled his following the Dugu tribe.

translations.literal: Shili fathered Wuli.
translations.idiomatic: Shili fathered Wuli.

translations.literal: Two sons: Qubei and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Wuli had two sons: Qubei and Meng.

translations.literal: Meng fathered Fulun.
translations.idiomatic: Meng fathered Fulun.

sentences.zh: 副論生路孤，路孤生眷，眷生羅辰，從後魏孝文徙洛陽，為河南人，初以其部為氏，位定州刺史、永安公。

translations.literal: Fulun fathered Lugu; Lugu fathered Juan; Juan fathered Luochen; following Later Wei Emperor Xiaowen he moved to Luoyang and became a man of Henan; at first they took their tribe as clan name; he held the post of Inspector of Ding Prefecture and Duke of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fulun fathered Lugu, Lugu fathered Juan, and Juan fathered Luochen, who followed Emperor Xiaowen to Luoyang as a Henan resident, first taking the tribe as surname; he was Inspector of Ding Prefecture and Duke of Yong'an.

translations.literal: He fathered Duke Zhen of Yong'an Wanling, Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Luochen fathered Wanling, Minister of Justice and Duke Zhen of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 萬齡生稽，字延平，鎮東將軍、文公。

translations.literal: Wanling fathered Ji, styled Yanping, General Who Guards the East and Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Wanling fathered Ji, styled Yanping, General Who Guards the East and Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 稽生鎮東將軍歸，歸生冀。

translations.literal: Ji fathered General Who Guards the East Gui; Gui fathered Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ji fathered Gui, General Who Guards the East; Gui fathered Ji.

translations.literal: Of the Dugu clan there was one chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Dugu clan produced one chancellor.

translations.literal: Sun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun.

sentences.zh: 三公三師李柳城李氏，世為契丹酋長，後徙京兆萬年。

translations.literal: Three Dukes and Three Preceptors: the Li of Liucheng, for generations chieftains of the Khitan, later moved to Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Three Dukes and Three Preceptors: the Li of Liucheng, for generations Khitan chieftains, later moved to Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 武威李氏，本安氏，出自姬姓。

translations.literal: Wuwei Li clan, originally the An clan, came from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuwei Li, originally the An clan, traced their origin to the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 黃帝生昌意，昌意次子安，居于西方，自號安息國。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor fathered Changyi; Changyi's second son An lived in the west and styled himself the state of Parthia.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor fathered Changyi; Changyi's second son An lived in the west and called his realm Parthia.

sentences.zh: 後漢末，遣子世高入朝，因居洛陽。

translations.literal: At the end of Later Han his son Shigao entered court and settled in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Han, his son Shigao came to court and settled in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 晉、魏間，家于安定，後徙遼左，以避亂又徙武威。

translations.literal: Between Jin and Wei the family lived in Anding, later moved to Liaodong, and to escape turmoil again moved to Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Between Jin and Wei they lived in Anding, later moved to Liaodong, then to Wuwei to escape turmoil.

sentences.zh: 後魏有難陀孫婆羅，周、隋間，居涼州武威為薩寶。

translations.literal: Later Wei had Nantuo's grandson Poluo; between Zhou and Sui they lived in Wuwei in Liang Prefecture as Sabao.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Wei came Poluo, grandson of Nantuo; between Zhou and Sui the family lived at Wuwei in Liang Prefecture as Sabao.

translations.literal: He fathered Xinggui and Xiuren.
translations.idiomatic: He fathered Xinggui and Xiuren.

translations.literal: To Baoyu the surname Li was granted.
translations.idiomatic: By Baoyu's time the clan received the surname Li.

translations.idiomatic: The Goryeo Li clan:

sentences.zh: 柳城李氏，本奚族，不知何氏。

translations.literal: Liucheng Li clan, originally the Xi tribe, unknown original surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Liucheng Li, originally Xi, of unknown original clan.

sentences.zh: 至寶臣為張鏁高養子，冒姓張氏，後賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: To Baochen, adopted son of Zhang Suo, he bore the Zhang surname; later the Li surname was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen was adopted by Zhang Suo and bore Zhang; later he received the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 鷄田李氏，本河曲部落稽阿跌之族，至光進賜姓李。

translations.literal: Jitian Li clan, originally the Hequ tribal A'die clan; to Guangjin the Li surname was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Jitian Li descended from the Hequ A'die tribe; Guangjin received the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 范陽李氏，自云常山愍王之後。

translations.literal: Fanyang Li clan, themselves claiming descent from Prince Min of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Fanyang Li claimed descent from Prince Min of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 代北李氏，本沙陀部落，姓朱邪氏。

translations.literal: Saibei Li clan, originally the Shatuo tribe, surname Zhuye.
translations.idiomatic: The Saibei Li were originally Shatuo of the Zhuye surname.

sentences.zh: 至國昌，賜姓李，附鄭王屬籍。

translations.literal: To Guochang the surname Li was granted and he was attached to the register of the Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guochang received the surname Li and was entered in the Prince of Zheng's clan register.

sentences.zh: 李氏三公七人，三師二人。

translations.literal: Of the Li clan there were seven Three Dukes and two Three Preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: The Li produced seven Three Dukes and two Three Preceptors.

translations.idiomatic: The Liucheng Li produced Guangbi;

translations.idiomatic: the Wuwei Li produced Baoyu;

translations.idiomatic: the Goryeo Li produced Zhengyi.

translations.idiomatic: Also among the Liucheng Li was Baochen;

translations.literal: the Fanyang Li had Zaiyi;
translations.idiomatic: the Fanyang Li produced Zaiyi;

translations.literal: the Saibei Li had Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: the Saibei Li produced Keyong.

translations.literal: Wang: Yingzhou Wang clan, originally a Goryeo people.
translations.idiomatic: Wang: the Yingzhou Wang were originally Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 太原王氏，世居祁縣，後徙平州，至縉，從侯希逸南遷，遂居河內溫縣。

translations.literal: Taiyuan Wang clan, for generations lived in Qi county, later moved to Ping Prefecture; to Jin they followed Hou Xiyi south and thus lived in Wen county, Henei.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiyuan Wang lived in Qi county for generations, later moved to Ping Prefecture; under Jin they followed Hou Xiyi south to Wen county in Henei.

sentences.zh: 安東王氏，本阿布思之族，世隸安東都護府，曰五哥之，左武衞將軍，生末怛活。

translations.literal: Andong Wang clan, originally the Abu Si tribe, for generations subordinate to the Protectorate of Andong, called Wugezhi, Left Guards General, fathered Motohuo.
translations.idiomatic: The Andong Wang were originally the Abu Si tribe, long under the Andong Protectorate; Wugezhi, Left Guards General, fathered Motohuo.

sentences.zh: 王氏三公二人，三師一人。

translations.literal: Of the Wang clan there were two Three Dukes and one Three Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The Wang produced two Three Dukes and one Three Preceptor.

translations.idiomatic: The Yingzhou Wang produced Sili;

translations.idiomatic: the Andong Wang produced Rong.

translations.literal: The Tian clan—Tian—came from the Gui surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Tian clan traced its origin to the Gui surname.

sentences.zh: 陳厲公子完，字敬仲，仕齊，初有采地，因號田氏。

translations.literal: Prince Wan, son of Duke Li of Chen, styled Jing Zhong, served Qi; at first he had a fief and therefore was styled the Tian clan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wan of Chen, styled Jing Zhong, served Qi; he first held a fief and thus became known as the Tian clan.

translations.literal: It is also said "Chen" and "Tian" are close in sound.
translations.idiomatic: Another account notes that "Chen" and "Tian" sound alike.

sentences.zh: 至田和篡齊為諸侯，九世至王建，為秦所滅。

translations.literal: When Tian He usurped Qi to become a feudal lord, through nine generations to Wang Jian it was destroyed by Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian He seized Qi as a feudal lord, the line ran nine generations to Wang Jian before Qin destroyed it.

sentences.zh: 漢興，諸田徙陽陵，後徙北平。

translations.literal: At Han's rise the various Tian were moved to Yangling, later to Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Han the Tian clans were relocated to Yangling, later to Beiping.

translations.literal: Wei Gentleman-advisor Tian Chou, styled Zitai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gentleman-advisor Tian Chou was styled Zitai.

translations.literal: The twenty-second-generation descendant Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two generations later came Jing.

translations.literal: Of the Tian clan there was one Three Duke.
translations.idiomatic: The Tian clan produced one Three Duke.

translations.literal: Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi.

translations.literal: The Wu clan—Wu—came from the Ji surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu clan traced its origin to the Ji surname.

sentences.zh: 黃帝之後，少昊氏以烏鳥名官，以世功命氏。

translations.literal: After the Yellow Emperor, Shaohao took bird names for offices and granted clan names by hereditary merit.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yellow Emperor, Shaohao named his offices after birds and granted surnames according to hereditary achievement.

sentences.zh: 齊有烏之餘，裔孫世居北方，號烏洛侯，後徙張掖。

translations.literal: In Qi there was Yu of Wu; a descendant for generations lived in the north, styled Wuluohou, later moved to Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi was Yu of Wu; descendants lived in the north for generations as Wuluohou, later moving to Zhangye.

translations.literal: Of the Wu clan there was one Three Duke.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu clan produced one Three Duke.

translations.literal: Chongyin.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin.

sentences.zh: 【結】唐宰相三百六十九人，凡九十八族。

translations.literal: 【Conclusion】Tang chancellors numbered three hundred sixty-nine persons, altogether ninety-eight clans.
translations.idiomatic: 【Conclusion】Tang chancellors numbered three hundred sixty-nine men from ninety-eight clans in all.
